data.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 9:52PM EDT until October 23 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward County and Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, from 3 AM EDT Wednesday
through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding is expected around
high tide.
data.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
727 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 725 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

 - Hazardous marine conditions continue today for both the
   Atlantic and Gulf waters. 

 - High risk of rip currents continues for the Atlantic beaches,
   and will likely last at least into early next week. In
   addition, high surf conditions continue for the Palm Beaches.

 - Minor coastal flooding expected to begin today around high 
   tide along the east coast. Moderate to potentially major 
   coastal flooding is possible this weekend.

 - Heavy rain, isolated flash flooding, and windy conditions are
   forecast for this weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 100 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Surface high pressure will remain to our north today and Thursday. 
At the upper levels, height falls will continue as a trough builds 
across the state and the ridge over the middle of the country starts 
to nose eastward. Mainly dry conditions are expected the next couple 
of days, with plenty of dry air in the mid and upper levels of the 
atmosphere. Just enough low level moisture will be in place for 
occasional coastal showers across the east coast metro, especially 
during the evening and overnight hours. 

High temps today and Thursday will be in the low to middle 80s for 
most, with some upper 80s over SW FL. Low temps tonight will range 
from the middle 60s around the lake to the lower 70s near the 
Atlantic coast.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 208 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Forecast gets interesting as we head into the weekend and into early 
next week. A 500 mb low will form in the vicinity of Cuba and strong 
surface high pressure will be in place over the northeast US. Deep 
moisture will be in place over SE FL for multiple days with PWAT 
values increasing to 1.8-2.0 inches. Rounds of heavy rainfall appear 
likely especially on Saturday and Sunday, but may continue into 
Monday as well. Mean rainfall totals from Friday through Monday show 
3-6 inches for the east coast metro, with worst case scenario values 
over 10 inches possible. Given the peak of the current king tide 
cycle is also this weekend, the potential exists for some serious 
flooding concerns across the metro and other poor drainage 
locations along the coast. Should the forecast remain the same 
over the coming days, Flood headlines would be very likely. 

In addition to the heavy rain threat, the tightening of the pressure 
gradient this weekend across FL will result in breezy NE winds, 
with gusts of 30-40 mph likely, especially along the coast. 

Conditions will improve for Tuesday into mid week as the upper low 
opens up and lifts up to the northeast and drier air moves back into 
the area. 

Temperatures during the extended period will see high temps in the 
low to mid 80s each day and lows in the 60s/70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 725 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

VFR conditions will prevail throughout the forecast period. NW
winds early this morning will gradually become NE after 15z and 
will range between 10 to 15 kts through the afternoon hours. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 100 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Hazardous seas will continue in the Atlantic waters the rest of the 
week with seas of 6-9 ft. NE winds 15-20 kts. In the Gulf waters, 
hazardous winds early in the day will become cautionary by this 
evening. 

Hazardous winds and seas return for all local waters this weekend 
into early next week as the pressure gradient tightens across the 
area. Gale force winds are possible in both the Atlantic and Gulf 
waters this weekend. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 100 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

A high risk of rip currents will remain for the Atlantic beaches 
through early next week. In addition, dangerous waves of 6-10 ft in 
the surf zone are likely in the Palm Beaches through early next 
week. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Issued at 100 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026 

We're beginning to come out of an ebb in the astronomical tides 
as we head towards the full moon and peak of the tide forecasts 
late this weekend and into early next week. Observed water-levels 
are already over-performing predictions and we'll likely begin 
reaching Minor flooding thresholds this morning at all of our 
east coast tidal stations. It's likely we'll also reach Moderate 
flooding levels by as early as Friday but certainly over the 
weekend; even before the peak of the King Tide cycle. It's not out
of the question that Palm Beach county may even reach Major 
flooding levels at the peak of the King Tide. The normal King 
Tides are complicated by the fact that we'll be dealing with a 
complex upper/surface low pressure pattern that will feature an 
approaching front from the north and convection rising out of the 
Caribbean from the south. This will likely increase the onshore 
wind component and magnify the already high tides. This is 
somewhat accounted for in the predictions mentioned above, but 
only crudely. Furthermore, the potential for heavy rainfall during
periods of high tide is also something to be aware of that could 
further aggravate coastal flooding. In short, we're heading into 
what could be a rather impactful period for coastal flooding and 
sensitive locations should consider preparations.

&&

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Offshore of the East Coast of the United States (AL93):
A storm-force non-tropical low pressure area located a few hundred 
miles off the mid-Atlantic United States coast is producing some 
shower and thunderstorm activity primarily west and northwest of its 
center. Over the next day or two, the low could gradually lose its 
frontal features while it moves slowly north-northeastward over the 
Gulf Stream, allowing the system to possibly develop subtropical 
characteristics. By Friday, the system is expected to accelerate 
northeastward away from the the eastern United States, and 
environmental conditions are expected to become unfavorable for 
additional subtropical or tropical development. 

Regardless of the status of the system, high winds, coastal 
flooding, and dangerous surf are expected along portions of the U.S. 
East Coast during the next few days. For more information, please 
consult statements and warnings from local National Weather Service 
offices and the Weather Prediction Center, along with the High Seas 
Forecasts and the Storm Warnings issued by the National Weather 
Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php

$$
